fields.why: The Summary singles out large increases among ages <=10 and 11-14 against 15-24, comparing the period effect across three age groups. The CI-vs-1 tests of visit ratios within each age group make no entry by themselves (rule 6), but this cross-age comparison does.
Sex is a two-group (female-to-male) contrast; age is the only SPD with 3 groups.
No test is run across the age groups; the age-specific visit ratios are only set side by side.

brief_issues: Rule 6 does not say whether contrasting the size of a within-level non-SPD effect across 3+ SPD levels (here: larger increases in some age groups) earns a side-by-side entry; A's reading follows the ranking pattern, but no entry is also arguable.
